full_judgment: 2. Circumstances giving rise to this air peal may be described as follows: Respondent as plaintiff filed O.C. Suit No. 225 of 1960 in the Court of Munsif, Rajshahi, for recovery of khas possession of the suit land by ejecting the appellant defendant. He claimed the appellant to be his tenant from month to month in respect of the suit premises. The appellant denied the landlord-tenant relationship with the respondent and set up a claim of his independent title on the basis of purchase. The suit land consists of 3 Plots. Nos. 25, 26 and 27 recorded under three separate C.S. Khatians, Plot No. 24 belonged to Kalicharan; plot No. 27 belonged to Shashi Bhushan and Plot No. 25 belonged to Swarna Baishnabi. According to the respondent, Kali Charan purchased the other two plots, got his name mutated in the landlord's sherista, paid rent for those plots till his death, and after him his son, Pati Ram, defendant No. 2, inherited the property and possessed it in the same way. Defendant No. 2 executed a Power of Attorney dated 2-1-51. Ext. 1, in favour of one Sekandar giving him full power to transfer the suit land and Sekandar accordingly transferred the suit land consisting of all the three plots to the plaintiff by executing a registered sale-deed dated 9-4-51, Ext. 2. Plaintiff immediately took possession, constructed a few huts on the land and inducted thereon defendant No. 1 as a monthly tenant at a rental of Tk. 10/- from Chaitra 1358 B.S. The defendant after paying rent for a few months started defaulting and during "Rent-roll Operation" unsuccessfully tried to get his name recorded in the khatian as owner of the suit premises. The Revenue authorities after rejections recorded the plaintiff's name in the S.A. Khatian. Thereafter defendant No. 1 procured a sale-deed from Golap Sundari, Shashi, Bhusan's wife, and therewith tried to assert his title. The plaintiff served a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act upon defendant No. 1 and thereby terminating the tenancy, filed the suit for ejectment. Contention of defendant No.1 was that he was never a tenant of the plaintiff, but that he had first entered into plot. No. 27 with permission of Golap Sundari in 1949 erected the huts thereon and entered into an agreement with her for sale of this plot on 26-11-56 and thereafter, by a registered sale-deed dated 3-8-59 purchased the plot. As to plot No. 26 which was inherited by Pati Ram from Kali Charan, defendant No. 1 claimed that by an agreement with Pati Ram, for sale he got possession of this plot from 1949, but Pati Ram subsequently proved faithless, sided with the plaintiff, and disowned the agreement. As to plot No. 25, his claim is that as it was lying vacant he took over its possession. He denied the plaintiff's title to the suit premises and particularly denied that he was inducted by plaintiff as a monthly tenant.
